blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.18
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.18

blocks.text: विद्याऽविनाशे जन्मविनाशः
blocks.directed: [slowly] विद्याऽविनाशे जन्मविनाशः

blocks.text: Vidyā’vināśe janmavināśaḥ.
blocks.directed: Vidyā’vināśe janmavināśaḥ.

blocks.text: When knowledge does not perish, birth comes to an end.
blocks.directed: When knowledge does not perish, birth comes to an end.

blocks.text: Congratulations, You’ve Cancelled Your Saṃsāra Subscription.
blocks.directed: Congratulations, You’ve Cancelled Your Saṃsāra Subscription.

blocks.text: Now this is one of the most important sūtras in the entire section.
blocks.directed: Now this is one of the most important sūtras in the entire section.

blocks.text: And there is an absolutely crucial detail in the Sanskrit.
blocks.directed: And there is an absolutely crucial detail in the Sanskrit.

blocks.text: Avināśe.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Avināśe.

blocks.text: Not vināśe.
blocks.directed: Not vināśe.

blocks.text: The difference is one vowel.
blocks.directed: The difference is one vowel.

blocks.text: But that vowel changes the entire meaning.
blocks.directed: But that vowel changes the entire meaning.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack it.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack it.

blocks.text: Vidyā — knowledge.
blocks.directed: Vidyā — knowledge.

blocks.text: Avināśa — non-destruction, imperishability.
blocks.directed: Avināśa — non-destruction, imperishability.

blocks.text: Janma — birth.
blocks.directed: Janma — birth.

blocks.text: Vināśa — destruction, cessation.
blocks.directed: Vināśa — destruction, cessation.

blocks.text: So the sense is:
blocks.directed: [short pause] So the sense is:

blocks.text: When liberating knowledge remains undestroyed, birth is extinguished.
blocks.directed: When liberating knowledge remains undestroyed, birth is extinguished.

blocks.text: Now, why is this so significant?
blocks.directed: Now, why is this so significant?

blocks.text: Because we’ve already seen what happens when supreme knowledge subsides.
blocks.directed: Because we’ve already seen what happens when supreme knowledge subsides.

blocks.text: Book II ended with the warning:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Book II ended with the warning:

blocks.text: Vidyāsaṃhāre tadutthasvapnadarśanam.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Vidyāsaṃhāre tadutthasvapnadarśanam.

blocks.text: When pure knowledge subsides, dreamlike differentiation arises again.
blocks.directed: When pure knowledge subsides, dreamlike differentiation arises again.

blocks.text: The practitioner may have attained an extraordinary recognition.
blocks.directed: The practitioner may have attained an extraordinary recognition.

blocks.text: But if that recognition does not remain established, the conditions of limitation can return.
blocks.directed: But if that recognition does not remain established, the conditions of limitation can return.

blocks.text: And now the complementary statement appears.
blocks.directed: And now the complementary statement appears.

blocks.text: When innate liberating knowledge does not disappear, birth is ended.
blocks.directed: When innate liberating knowledge does not disappear, birth is ended.

blocks.text: But what does Kṣemarāja mean by birth?
blocks.directed: But what does Kṣemarāja mean by birth?

blocks.text: He gives a specific answer.
blocks.directed: He gives a specific answer.

blocks.text: He is not merely referring to the biological event of emerging from a womb.
blocks.directed: He is not merely referring to the biological event of emerging from a womb.

blocks.text: He refers to the conditioned complex of body, senses and other constituents of embodied existence, produced through karma in conjunction with ignorance.
blocks.directed: He refers to the conditioned complex of body, senses and other constituents of embodied existence, produced through karma in conjunction with ignorance.

blocks.text: And he associates this with suffering.
blocks.directed: And he associates this with suffering.

blocks.text: In other words, birth here belongs to the larger machinery of saṃsāra.
blocks.directed: In other words, birth here belongs to the larger machinery of saṃsāra.

blocks.text: Repeated conditioned existence.
blocks.directed: Repeated conditioned existence.

blocks.text: And the question is:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And the question is:

blocks.text: What sustains it?
blocks.directed: What sustains it?

blocks.text: Within Kṣemarāja’s account, ignorance and karma participate in the perpetuation of embodied bondage.
blocks.directed: Within Kṣemarāja’s account, ignorance and karma participate in the perpetuation of embodied bondage.

blocks.text: The individual experiences itself as a finite agent.
blocks.directed: The individual experiences itself as a finite agent.

blocks.text: Acts within the field of differentiation.
blocks.directed: Acts within the field of differentiation.

blocks.text: Undergoes the results of action.
blocks.directed: Undergoes the results of action.

blocks.text: And remains bound within the cycle.
blocks.directed: And remains bound within the cycle.

blocks.text: But when sahajavidyā, innate knowledge, shines continually, the underlying ignorance is overcome.
blocks.directed: But when sahajavidyā, innate knowledge, shines continually, the underlying ignorance is overcome.

blocks.text: The binding conditions of rebirth are thereby brought to an end.
blocks.directed: The binding conditions of rebirth are thereby brought to an end.

blocks.text: Now, there’s something fascinating here.
blocks.directed: Now, there’s something fascinating here.

blocks.text: Because from the Trika standpoint, liberation doesn’t require universal consciousness to become something other than itself.
blocks.directed: Because from the Trika standpoint, liberation doesn’t require universal consciousness to become something other than itself.

blocks.text: Śiva doesn’t need to be manufactured.
blocks.directed: Śiva doesn’t need to be manufactured.

blocks.text: Nor does the realised yogi need to acquire an entirely foreign divine substance.
blocks.directed: Nor does the realised yogi need to acquire an entirely foreign divine substance.

blocks.text: The transformation concerns the conditions under which consciousness experiences itself as limited.
blocks.directed: The transformation concerns the conditions under which consciousness experiences itself as limited.

blocks.text: And this is why knowledge is so central.
blocks.directed: And this is why knowledge is so central.

blocks.text: Not because collecting philosophical information somehow cancels karma like paying an overdue parking ticket.
blocks.directed: Not because collecting philosophical information somehow cancels karma like paying an overdue parking ticket.

blocks.text: But because genuine recognition undermines the ignorance sustaining the contracted condition.
blocks.directed: But because genuine recognition undermines the ignorance sustaining the contracted condition.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja isn’t talking merely about knowing the correct sentence.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja isn’t talking merely about knowing the correct sentence.

blocks.text: Imagine somebody saying:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Imagine somebody saying:

blocks.text: “I have read that consciousness is the Self.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I have read that consciousness is the Self.”

blocks.text: Wonderful.
blocks.directed: Wonderful.

blocks.text: Congratulations.
blocks.directed: Congratulations.

blocks.text: You’ve read five Sanskrit words.
blocks.directed: You’ve read five Sanskrit words.

blocks.text: But that doesn’t mean the deeply rooted structures of limited identification have necessarily ceased.
blocks.directed: But that doesn’t mean the deeply rooted structures of limited identification have necessarily ceased.

blocks.text: The vidyā in question is transformative knowledge — the stable manifestation of one’s true conscious nature.
blocks.directed: The vidyā in question is transformative knowledge — the stable manifestation of one’s true conscious nature.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja insists on its continuity.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja insists on its continuity.

blocks.text: Not a temporary glimpse.
blocks.directed: Not a temporary glimpse.

blocks.text: Not a particularly impressive meditation.
blocks.directed: Not a particularly impressive meditation.

blocks.text: Not a brief experience that you subsequently spend thirty years telling strangers about.
blocks.directed: Not a brief experience that you subsequently spend thirty years telling strangers about.

blocks.text: Stable recognition.
blocks.directed: Stable recognition.

blocks.text: He cites tantric sources that associate seeing the whole universe as pervaded by Śiva with the cessation of further birth.
blocks.directed: He cites tantric sources that associate seeing the whole universe as pervaded by Śiva with the cessation of further birth.

blocks.text: And he explicitly includes the claim that the liberated person is not reborn after bodily death.
blocks.directed: And he explicitly includes the claim that the liberated person is not reborn after bodily death.

blocks.text: That is the traditional soteriological assertion, not an empirically verified account of what happens after death. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: That is the traditional soteriological assertion, not an empirically verified account of what happens after death. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now consider the elegance of the progression.
blocks.directed: Now consider the elegance of the progression.

blocks.text: At 3.16, the yogi enters the Great Lake.
blocks.directed: At 3.16, the yogi enters the Great Lake.

blocks.text: At 3.17, manifestation is recognised through the power of consciousness.
blocks.directed: At 3.17, manifestation is recognised through the power of consciousness.

blocks.text: At 3.18, that recognition, when uninterrupted, is said to end the necessity of rebirth.
blocks.directed: At 3.18, that recognition, when uninterrupted, is said to end the necessity of rebirth.

blocks.text: The lake.
blocks.directed: The lake.

blocks.text: The universe.
blocks.directed: The universe.

blocks.text: Liberation.
blocks.directed: Liberation.

blocks.text: Not bad for three sūtras.
blocks.directed: Not bad for three sūtras.

blocks.text: But there’s a catch.
blocks.directed: But there’s a catch.

blocks.text: And it’s a rather magnificent catch.
blocks.directed: And it’s a rather magnificent catch.

blocks.text: Because even after recognising the supreme nature of consciousness, the yogi can become inattentive.
blocks.directed: Because even after recognising the supreme nature of consciousness, the yogi can become inattentive.

blocks.text: And when that happens, some very powerful ladies are apparently waiting to seize control of the entire operation.
blocks.directed: And when that happens, some very powerful ladies are apparently waiting to seize control of the entire operation.

blocks.text: The Mothers.
blocks.directed: The Mothers.

blocks.text: The goddesses of the phonemes.
blocks.directed: The goddesses of the phonemes.

blocks.text: The divine powers that can liberate consciousness…
blocks.directed: The divine powers that can liberate consciousness…

blocks.text: Or plunge it straight back into bondage.
blocks.directed: Or plunge it straight back into bondage.

blocks.text: And, oh, they’re going to be trouble.
blocks.directed: And, oh, they’re going to be trouble.
